facts.text: This movie was shot for about $50,000 in 1985 as 'Georgia County Lock-up.' Troma later added $125,000 to retool it for theaters.
Director Eric Louzil found his location on the evening news: Ely, Nevada's 'Rent A Town' program, created after the nearby Robinson Mine closed.
Producer Lloyd Kaufman said the original script was retooled during production into a 'feminist action film.'
Heavy metal band Grim Reaper supplies two songs here. One reviewer counted 'Rock You to Hell' at least 13 times before giving up.
The film played the Cannes Film Festival in May 1987, then waited until February 19, 1988 for its theatrical release.
Melanie Coll, who plays Gillian Kaites, never made another film. This was her only screen role.
About 30 percent of the film was shot in Ely, Nevada. The rest was shot at studios in California.
Filming in Ely began July 8, 1985, with a 30-person crew. Local councilmember Carl Stanek landed a small role.
Louzil often cast adult film actresses. He said they work nude without complaint and show up on time, because sex is a business to them.
Louzil's own house doubles as the home of Gillian Kaites, and Jud's van belonged to Louzil too.
The police station scenes were shot in a rundown coffee shop.
Dee 'Queen Kong' Booher, who plays Big Eddie, was a professional wrestler. The film's wrestling scene was choreographed by William J. Kulzer, who plays Sheriff Coale.
Michelle Bauer, a well-known B-movie scream queen, appears as Jackie.
The LA Times said it 'looks as though it cost almost nothing to make. That's a relief.' It also joked that inmates revolt over hearing the same two Grim Reaper songs on repeat.
Production budgets are slippery: Wikipedia lists the budget as $1.5 million, but says the film was actually made for $50,000.
The New York Times' Caryn James said the worst exploitation films masquerade as spoofs, luring 'innocent but otherwise intelligent people to the theater.'
A critic noted Kevin Costner's career survived Eric Louzil's direction in 'Sizzle Beach, U.S.A.' but doubted Coll's would.
The 1987 UK video release lost 5 minutes 34 seconds, including women fighting and the chalet 'snuff movie' scene.
The 2003 Hollywood DVD restored most UK cuts, but 24 seconds were still trimmed to remove nudity during a rape scene.
Louzil later directed Class of Nuke 'Em High Part II and Part III, and this film gets name-checked in Part 3 and Tromeo and Juliet.
It's also referenced in The Toxic Avenger Part III and in the 2013 VHS documentary Rewind This!
Actress Amy Lyndon is credited as 'Mary Robinson' but actually plays Amy, the girl who flashes the black van.
Louzil said they made over $2 million, because in the VHS days people paid high prices for videos.
Some of the jail scenes were shot at the Lincoln Heights Jail in Los Angeles.
A 2005 Film Threat review called it a 'by-the-books women in prison movie,' with a snuff film subplot and a British heavy metal soundtrack.
The 2014 Vinegar Syndrome DVD includes Louzil's commentary and a Lloyd Kaufman interview. A later Troma Blu-ray adds a message from Eli Roth.
The TMDB tagline: 'Bras & brawls behind prison walls!'
